sections.heading: C — Rules of the road, part two: turn signals, left and right turns, turns on red, roundabouts and U-turns, lane use, passing and being passed, backing, parking rules and no-parking zones
sections.markdown:
## C — Rules of the road, part two: turn signals, left and right turns, turns on red, roundabouts and U-turns, lane use, passing and being passed, backing, parking rules and no-parking zones
Knowledge domain: the second half of the Tennessee rules of the road — when and how to signal, how to make left and right turns on two-way and one-way streets, when turns on red are allowed, how to use roundabouts and when U-turns are banned, which lane to drive in, how to pass and be passed safely, how to back up, and where and how you may park.

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Turn on your turn signal at least 50 feet before a turn or lane change. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
If you plan to turn just past an intersection, wait until you are in the intersection to signal, so no one thinks you are turning at it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
Do not use your turn signal to wave a driver behind you around, or to repeat the signals of cars ahead of you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
If you are in the wrong lane for a turn, go on to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane there. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
While waiting to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight, because a rear-end hit with the wheels turned can push you into oncoming traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
Do not brake or press the clutch during the turn itself, and do not shift gears in the intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
When two drivers meet at an intersection and both turn left, each turns to the left of the other. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A02
For a left turn from a two-way street, approach in the lane next to the center line, then turn into the first lane just right of the center line of the new street, never wide into the right lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A02
If the light turns yellow while you are waiting to turn left, do not pull into the intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A02
Center lines are yellow on two-way streets and white on one-way streets. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A02
Turning left onto a one-way street, turn sharply into the first lane, the one nearest the left curb. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A02
On a one-way street, approach a left turn from the lane farthest to the left. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A02
Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street is never allowed on a red light. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A03
In a multiple turn lane setup, the second lane may make the same turn as the first only when a sign or pavement marking allows it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A03
On a right turn, do not swing wide to the left; stay close to the right curb and turn into the lane nearest the right curb. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A03
Large trucks and buses must swing wide when turning, so never pass one on the right if it may be turning right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A03
Tennessee allows a right turn on red, and a left turn on red from a one-way street onto a one-way street going left, unless a sign forbids it, after a full stop and yielding. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A04
Always travel counterclockwise, to the right, around a roundabout, and yield to vehicles already circulating before entering. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A04
Roundabout speeds are usually posted at 15 to 25 mph, you may not pass inside a multi-lane roundabout, and you signal right to exit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A04
You may not make a U-turn at an intersection controlled by a signal or officer, or anywhere you cannot see 500 feet of traffic both ways. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A04
U-turns are also banned between intersections in a city and wherever signs or markings forbid them; driving around the block is safer. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A04
U-turns on interstates are illegal, and median emergency crossovers are only for emergency and maintenance vehicles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A04
On a road with no center line, give oncoming drivers at least half of the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A04
White on your right, yellow on your left: if the yellow line is on your right, you are on the wrong side and must pull over at once. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A04
The center lane of a two-way road with three or five lanes is used only for left turns. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A05
On a divided highway always use the road on the right, and cross the median only at an authorized crossover or intersection or when directed. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A05
Red reflectors facing you on the lane lines mean you are driving the wrong way and could hit someone head on. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A05
A shared center turn lane is only for left turns from either direction, may not be used for passing, and may not be driven in for more than 300 feet. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A05
When drivers from opposite directions enter a shared center turn lane, the first one in has the right-of-way. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A06
Over reversible lanes, a green arrow means you may use the lane, a red X means you may not, a flashing yellow X means turns only, and a steady yellow X means leave the lane soon. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A06
Reserved lanes marked by a white diamond are for buses, bicycles or HOV car pools only, though you may cross one to turn within the next half block. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A06
To change lanes, check your mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder toward your move, check blind spots, and then move over gradually. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A07
Before passing, assume that any oncoming vehicle you can see is too close, and when in doubt stay in your lane. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A07
Return to your lane after passing only when you can see the whole passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, and then cancel your signal. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A07
Passing several vehicles at once is not illegal in Tennessee but is generally unsafe, and should only be tried if you can be back in your lane 100 feet before a no-passing marking or oncoming car. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A07
You may pass on the right only when the car ahead is turning left or the road has room for two or more moving lanes your way, and never by leaving the pavement. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A08
Do not pass near an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, or when approaching a hill or curve. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A08
Never pass a car that has stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk, a frequent cause of pedestrian deaths. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F39 | anchor: A08
The end of a no-passing zone only means you can see farther; you still must judge whether passing is safe. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F40 | anchor: A08
When someone is passing you, stay in your lane, keep to the right and hold your speed, never speeding up to block them. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F41 | anchor: A08
Tennessee law requires at least 3 feet of space when passing a bicycle going your way, kept until you are safely past. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F42 | anchor: A09
If you cannot see a truck's side mirrors, its driver cannot see you, and lingering beside a truck keeps you in its blind spot. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F43 | anchor: A09
Never back into a travel lane except into a parallel parking space, and remember that backing is the maneuver new drivers most often fail on the road test. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F44 | anchor: A09
Backing from a driveway into an intersection is illegal, and so is backing up on an interstate. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F45 | anchor: A10
Outside city limits, park with all four wheels off the pavement if possible, leave at least 18 feet of road for traffic, and be visible for 200 feet both ways. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F46 | anchor: A10
On a downhill with a curb, or on any hill without a curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road; uphill with a curb, turn them away from the curb. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F47 | anchor: A10
Parking is illegal within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, within 20 feet of a crosswalk, within 30 feet of a traffic signal or stop sign, and within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0079]

Misconceptions: a signal never gives you the right-of-way; the end of a no-passing zone is not permission to pass; it is not illegal to pass several vehicles, only unsafe; uphill with a curb is the one hill case where the wheels point away from the curb; you cannot turn left on red onto a two-way street.
Mnemonics: fifty feet to signal; white on right, yellow on left; three feet for a bike; fifteen from a hydrant, twenty from a crosswalk, thirty from a signal, fifty from the tracks.
Glossary: roundabout means an intersection where traffic circles counterclockwise around a central island; shared center turn lane means a middle lane for left turns from both directions; reversible lane means a lane whose direction changes by time of day; crossover means a paved median opening on a divided four-lane highway.
Dynamic facts: local U-turn bans, reserved lane hours and HOV occupancy rules, parking fines and meter rules vary by place and time; confirm them on posted signs and official Tennessee sources.

corpus_stability.reason: The Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual says its content is current as of July 1, 2022 and its back cover carries one March 2025 print authorization; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year, but the content date is old, so freshness is held as debt rather than assumed.
